terms.definition: Application Programming Interface — a set of rules that allows two software systems to communicate with each other.
terms.example: When a weather app shows live data, it is calling a weather API to fetch that data from a remote server.

terms.definition: A fully managed AWS service that acts as the front door for all client requests to backend services — handling routing, auth, throttling, and monitoring.
terms.example: A mobile shopping app sends all requests to one API Gateway URL; the gateway routes /orders to one Lambda and /payments to another.

terms.definition: A verb in an HTTP request that tells the server what action to perform. Common methods: GET (read), POST (create), PUT (update), DELETE (remove).
terms.example: Clicking 'Place Order' triggers a POST request to /orders with the order details in the body.

terms.definition: In API Gateway, a resource is a path (like /users or /orders) that represents a backend component and maps to a specific backend service.
terms.example: The path /products is a resource that routes to the product catalog Lambda function.

terms.definition: A three-digit code in the server's response that indicates whether a request succeeded or failed, and why.
terms.example: 200 = success, 404 = not found, 500 = server error.

terms.definition: Status codes in the 200-299 range indicating the request was successful. 200 OK is the standard, 201 Created is returned after a successful POST.
terms.example: After creating a new user account, the server returns 201 Created.

terms.definition: Status codes in the 400-499 range indicating a client-side error — the problem is with the request sent, not the server.
terms.example: Sending a request to a path not defined in API Gateway returns 404 Not Found.

terms.definition: Status codes in the 500-599 range indicating a server-side error — the client's request was valid but the backend failed to process it.
terms.example: A bug in the Lambda function causes an unhandled exception, returning 500 Internal Server Error.

terms.definition: The most feature-rich API Gateway type — supports caching, request/response transformation, usage plans, API keys, and WAF integration.
terms.example: An enterprise API needing per-client rate limiting and response caching uses REST API type.

terms.definition: A lightweight, lower-cost API Gateway type designed for simple Lambda and HTTP proxy integrations with lower latency. Up to 71% cheaper than REST API.
terms.example: A startup's mobile backend uses HTTP API with JWT authorization for fast, cheap API calls to Lambda.

terms.definition: An API Gateway type that enables persistent, real-time bidirectional communication between clients and servers — the connection stays open continuously.
terms.example: A live chat application or collaborative editing tool uses WebSocket API so both client and server can send messages at any time.

terms.definition: A named reference to a specific deployment of your API in API Gateway — allows separate environments like dev, staging, and prod.
terms.example: The team tests new features in the 'dev' stage before deploying to the 'prod' stage serving real users.

terms.definition: API Gateway's mechanism for limiting the number of requests per second to protect the backend from being overwhelmed. Default: 10,000 RPS with 5,000 burst.
terms.example: A client sending 50,000 RPS gets throttled and receives 429 Too Many Requests responses.

terms.definition: A private connection between a VPC and a supported AWS service that keeps traffic within the AWS network — no internet, NAT Gateway, or VPN required.
terms.example: An EC2 in a private subnet accesses S3 without internet access by using a VPC Endpoint.

terms.definition: A type of VPC Endpoint that supports only S3 and DynamoDB, works by modifying the route table, and is free of charge.
terms.example: A data pipeline EC2 instance uses a Gateway Endpoint to read/write to S3 without incurring NAT Gateway costs.

terms.definition: A type of VPC Endpoint that uses AWS PrivateLink to create an ENI with a private IP inside your subnet, supporting most AWS services. Charged per hour and per GB.
terms.example: A private EC2 needs to call CloudWatch and Secrets Manager APIs — Interface Endpoints are created for each service.

terms.definition: Elastic Network Interface — a virtual network card in AWS. Interface Endpoints create an ENI with a private IP inside your subnet to handle PrivateLink traffic.
terms.example: When an Interface Endpoint for CloudWatch is created in subnet A, an ENI appears in subnet A with a private IP like 10.0.1.45.

terms.definition: The underlying technology powering Interface VPC Endpoints — enables private connectivity to AWS services and third-party SaaS using ENIs, without exposing traffic to the internet.
terms.example: A company connects to a SaaS vendor's service privately using PrivateLink without VPN or internet routing.

terms.definition: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing — a browser security mechanism that blocks web apps from calling APIs on a different domain unless the API explicitly allows it.
terms.example: A React app on myapp.com cannot call api.myapp.com unless CORS is enabled in API Gateway to allow that origin.

terms.definition: A custom Lambda function used for API Gateway authorization — it validates an incoming token and returns an IAM policy allowing or denying access.
terms.example: An API uses OAuth tokens; a Lambda Authorizer validates the JWT and returns a policy granting access to specific resources.

terms.definition: A REST API Gateway feature that defines rate limits and quota settings for individual API clients, identified by API keys.
terms.example: Free tier users get 100 API calls/day; premium users get 10,000/day — enforced via usage plans.
